## Repository Structure

| Directory | Purpose | Committed | Distributed |
|-----------|---------|-----------|-------------|
| `pack/` | Shippable doctrine artefacts (directives, tactics, agent profiles, toolguides, paradigms, procedures, styleguides, mission step contracts, templates, glossary, DRG) | ✅ | ✅ via `spec-kitty doctrine fetch` |
| `config/` | Dashboard and organisational management configuration (`domain-config.yaml`, `artifact-tags.yaml`, `org-bindings.yaml`). **Not** distributed. | ✅ | ❌ |
| `docs/` | **Documentation only.** Engineering notes, ADRs, HOW_TO_USE, OVERVIEW, SURFACES. No YAML configuration files. | ✅ | ❌ |
| `tools/` | Doctrine Organisational Management Dashboard (Angular + Express). Development-time utilities, validators, exporters. | ✅ | ❌ |
| `kitty-specs/` | Spec-kitty mission artefacts: specs, plans, work packages, status logs. | ✅ | ❌ |
| `.kittify/` | Spec-kitty project runtime. Charter committed; workspaces/runtime transient. | ✅ (charter) | ❌ |
| `gemini-agents/` | Generated Gemini Enterprise **chatbot** distribution surface — output of Gemini Bot Georgia from `pack/`. Committed but never hand-edited; **not** a DRG input. Separate population from `pack/agent_profiles/` (see `pack/README.md § Two agent surfaces`). | ✅ | ❌ |
| `work/` | Gitignored agent workspace: session logs, HiC escalation queue, learnings. | ❌ | ❌ |

### Decision rule for file placement

1. Shippable doctrine artefact → `pack/`
2. Dashboard/org enrichment YAML configuration → `config/`
3. Human-readable documentation → `docs/`
4. Build tool, dashboard app, exporter, validator → `tools/`
5. Mission spec, plan, or work package → `kitty-specs/`
6. Transient agent workspace → `work/` (gitignored)
7. Generated Gemini Enterprise chatbot artefact → `gemini-agents/` (generated by Gemini Bot Georgia from `pack/`; committed, never hand-edited, not a DRG input)

### Server environment variables

| Variable | Default | Controls |
|----------|---------|---------|
| `CONFIG_ROOT` | `<repo-root>/config` | Location of `domain-config.yaml`, `artifact-tags.yaml`, `org-bindings.yaml` |
| `DOCS_ROOT` | `<repo-root>/docs` | Location of documentation root (read-only) |
| `PACK_ROOT` | `<repo-root>/pack` | Location of the doctrine pack |

## Testing Standards

- Server-side: Vitest unit tests for CRUD services, route handlers, and validators. Frontend: Angular component testing for UI-critical paths. YAML artefacts: validated via spec-kitty doctrine pack validate before release. Acceptance: spec-kitty acceptance criteria in kitty-specs/<mission>/spec.md. No external service calls in unit tests (file I/O must be mockable).


## Quality Gates

- TypeScript must compile without errors (tsc --noEmit). Angular production build must succeed (ng build --configuration=production). All YAML artefacts pass spec-kitty schema validation before commit. No hard-coded hex values in CSS — always reference --rn-* brand tokens. No font-weight: bold (Regnology brand: 400/500 only). Atomic file writes (write to .tmp then rename) for all YAML persistence.


## Performance Benchmarks

- Dashboard server startup under 3 seconds on developer machine. Artifact list page renders within 1 second for packs up to 200 artefacts. No blocking synchronous file reads during request handling (use cached scans).


## Branch Strategy

- All work packages reviewed via spec-kitty review workflow before merging. Doctrine artefact changes require curator review for schema and DRG consistency. Dashboard changes require visual review against Regnology brand guide (docs/OVERVIEW.md §branding, regnology-docgen design-system/BRAND_OVERVIEW.md). Breaking changes to pack/ artefact schema require a DDR in docs/decisions/.

- Deployment constraints: Dashboard runs locally only — no cloud deployment, no authentication layer. Pack is distributed via git (spec-kitty doctrine fetch pulls from Bitbucket). No new npm or pip dependencies without explicit justification in a DDR or mission spec. CONFIG_ROOT env var controls the config/ path; DOCS_ROOT controls docs/ path.

## Policy Summary

- Intent: Maintain and distribute the Regnology Professional Services org doctrine pack for the spec-kitty framework. The primary deliverable is pack/ — a set of typed YAML governance artefacts (directives, tactics, agent profiles, toolguides, paradigms, procedures, styleguides, mission step contracts, templates) distributed to engagement repos via spec-kitty doctrine fetch. A secondary deliverable is the Doctrine Organisational Management Dashboard — a local Angular + Express webapp for inspecting, reviewing, validating, and enriching doctrine artefacts, including RACI-based organisational bindings.

- Languages/Frameworks: Primary artefact format: YAML (spec-kitty schema). Dashboard backend: TypeScript + Express (Node.js). Dashboard frontend: Angular 18+ (standalone components, TypeScript). Dashboard tests: Vitest (server unit tests). Python: spec-kitty CLI integration (validation scripts). Styling: SCSS with Regnology brand token system (--rn-* CSS custom properties).

- Testing: Server-side: Vitest unit tests for CRUD services, route handlers, and validators. Frontend: Angular component testing for UI-critical paths. YAML artefacts: validated via spec-kitty doctrine pack validate before release. Acceptance: spec-kitty acceptance criteria in kitty-specs/<mission>/spec.md. No external service calls in unit tests (file I/O must be mockable).

- Quality Gates: TypeScript must compile without errors (tsc --noEmit). Angular production build must succeed (ng build --configuration=production). All YAML artefacts pass spec-kitty schema validation before commit. No hard-coded hex values in CSS — always reference --rn-* brand tokens. No font-weight: bold (Regnology brand: 400/500 only). Atomic file writes (write to .tmp then rename) for all YAML persistence.

- Review Policy: All work packages reviewed via spec-kitty review workflow before merging. Doctrine artefact changes require curator review for schema and DRG consistency. Dashboard changes require visual review against Regnology brand guide (docs/OVERVIEW.md §branding, regnology-docgen design-system/BRAND_OVERVIEW.md). Breaking changes to pack/ artefact schema require a DDR in docs/decisions/.

- Performance Targets: Dashboard server startup under 3 seconds on developer machine. Artifact list page renders within 1 second for packs up to 200 artefacts. No blocking synchronous file reads during request handling (use cached scans).

- Deployment Constraints: Dashboard runs locally only — no cloud deployment, no authentication layer. Pack is distributed via git (spec-kitty doctrine fetch pulls from Bitbucket). No new npm or pip dependencies without explicit justification in a DDR or mission spec. CONFIG_ROOT env var controls the config/ path; DOCS_ROOT controls docs/ path.


## Project Directives

1. Respect risk boundaries: pack/ must never contain engagement-specific or organisational data. config/ must never be placed inside pack/ or distributed with the doctrine pack. No secrets, credentials, or PII committed to the repository. SPOC email addresses in org-bindings.yaml must match @regnology.net domain. Spec-kitty version upgrades require spec-kitty upgrade and charter resync.

2. Keep documentation synchronized with workflow and behavior changes.

## Terminology Canon

Use the glossary and mission contract names exactly when renaming or introducing terms. For this repository, `pack/` is the shippable doctrine pack, `config/` is non-distributed dashboard configuration, `dist/scripts/` is the installer distribution surface, and pack layer names must remain stable identifiers rather than prose aliases.

## Code Review Checklist

Before moving implementation work to review, verify that changed files stay within the work package's authoritative surface, required syntax/parser checks have been run, dry-run or other non-destructive evidence exists for installer ordering, and user-facing documentation matches the behavior implemented in scripts.

## Regression Vigilance

During terminology or slug cutovers, search for old identifiers in active operational surfaces and distinguish deliberate historical references from live fetch paths. For layered installer work, preserve base-then-overlay order across shell, PowerShell, README examples, archive coordinates, and post-install `spec-kitty doctrine fetch` commands.

## Amendment Process

Doctrine artefact additions/changes: raise as a mission in kitty-specs/ with a spec, then plan and implement via work packages. Directory convention changes: update docs/SURFACES.md and charter simultaneously. Breaking schema changes: require DDR before implementation.


## Exception Policy

Exceptions to quality gates must be documented as a comment in the relevant file and tracked in docs/engineering_notes/. Temporary deviations from the brand guide must be flagged with a TODO and an issue.
